about: Independently labelled ATLAS qualification corpus. Labels are written from the request's MEANING and the owner's policy below — never generated from code output. Each case runs through the real production path (scripts/dev/atlas-eval.ts). `defect` marks a case the current code is KNOWN to get wrong; fixing the defect must flip it, and the defect label is then removed in the same reviewed change.

titles: Account Executive includes Senior, Enterprise, Founding and verified equivalent titles (segment / seniority / level modifiers on the same role: Mid-Market, Commercial, Strategic, SMB, Sr., II, an 'AE' abbreviation).
Account Executive does NOT include SDR, BDR, Sales Representative or Account Manager by default.
An explicitly broad request ("salespeople", "sales roles") may use the broader sales-role family.
OR-connected roles must preserve every requested alternative.
geography: A hard geography passes only on a POSITIVE match of the company's evidenced location (HQ, or any location for presence).
A location resolved outside the requirement fails (when proven) — another country, or another state for a state requirement.
A requirement ATLAS cannot place (unknown place) never passes: unknown (pending).
Missing location evidence is unknown, never a pass.
policy.outcomes: pass = the requirement is proven; fail = proven otherwise; unknown = neither. `not_pass` accepts fail or unknown (both keep the company out of the qualified set).

geography.note: found by this corpus: the compiler rewrites the stated region to "United States" (company_profile.locations), narrowing a hard requirement; compiler scope, not in Stages 0-2
DE is Germany here, not Delaware: an ISO-colliding code is never read as a state
known limitation, fail-closed by design: CA is also Canada's ISO code, so it is never read as California; the company stays pending (unknown), never wrongly qualified
